items.title: Difference Between Traditional Programming and Machine Learning

source_refs.note: 'Difference Between Traditional Programming and Machine Learning' under topic 6.3, as printed (PDF 78-79, printed 74-75).

blocks.text: Traditional programming uses fixed rules written by programmers. The output is produced by following these rules. Machine learning uses data instead of fixed rules. The system learns rules automatically from data. In traditional programming, changes require new code. In machine learning, changes happen through new data. Machine learning handles complex problems better. It adapts to new situations. Figure 6.3 shows traditional programming vs machine learning

blocks.alt: Two panels. Traditional Programming (blue): a checklist labelled Fixed Rules, with arrows into a Rules box, which points down to a database labelled Data, with the bullets Databases and Spreadsheets. Machine Learning (orange): stacked databases point to a monitor showing results; below, Data leads into a neural network labelled Model, which leads to Output; bullet Patterns from Data.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.3: Traditional Programming vs Machine Learning (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.3)
blocks.long_description: The Machine Learning panel carries the labels Data, Output, Model and Output around its network picture; the monitor shows lines of text, ticks and a small line graph.
